account: Jean Hines, 83, collapsed at home and was taken to the Royal Berkshire Hospital, Reading, England, on a weekend in August. National Health Service (NHS) England's December 2025 statement gives no year, so 2025 is inferred. A scan carried out immediately on arrival, supported by the Brainomix AI imaging tool, identified a major stroke needing urgent specialist treatment. Within 25 minutes of reaching the emergency department she was on her way by ambulance to the John Radcliffe Hospital, Oxford. There she had a successful mechanical thrombectomy. She describes a very good physical recovery with no serious disabilities. NHS England states the Brainomix 360 Stroke tool is used in over 70 hospitals. It associates the tool with a 64-minute door-in-door-out reduction at primary stroke centers.

ai_role.statement: The AI-supported scan read identified the major stroke immediately on arrival, enabling a 25-minute door-in-door-out. The treatment itself (thrombectomy) was delivered by the Oxford team. The stroke would very likely have been diagnosed without AI. So the AI's contribution is the speed of decision and transfer. The Lancet Digital Health study (which has Brainomix co-authors alongside NHS lead authors) supports that at population level.

claim_basis: Sources: the makers' peer-reviewed study and the deployer's press release. The cited evidence includes no independent source and no finding by a regulator or court.

comparator.after: 4·6% (751 of 15 428 patients), a relative increase of 100%
comparator.against: thrombectomy rate at the same 26 hospitals before the software was implemented, with the 81 non-implementing hospitals as the background trend
comparator.quote: For evaluation sites, the pre-implementation endovascular thrombectomy rate was 2·3% (376 of 15 969 patients) and the post-implementation rate was 4·6% (751 of 15 428 patients), a relative increase of 100%. For non-evaluation sites, the pre-implementation rate was 1·6% (1431 of 88 712 patients) and the post-implementation rate was 2·6% (2410 of 89 900 patients), a relative increase of 62·5% (odds ratio [OR] for the interaction between site and time period 1·24 [95% CI 1·08-1·43]; p=0·0026).

fields.account: Jean Hines, 83, collapsed at home and was taken to the Royal Berkshire Hospital, Reading, England, on a weekend in August. National Health Service (NHS) England's December 2025 statement gives no year, so 2025 is inferred. A scan carried out immediately on arrival, supported by the Brainomix AI imaging tool, identified a major stroke needing urgent specialist treatment. Within 25 minutes of reaching the emergency department she was on her way by ambulance to the John Radcliffe Hospital, Oxford. There she had a successful mechanical thrombectomy. She describes a very good physical recovery with no serious disabilities. NHS England states the Brainomix 360 Stroke tool is used in over 70 hospitals. It associates the tool with a 64-minute door-in-door-out reduction at primary stroke centers.
